newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sets economic goals for year 2002.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sets economic goals for year 2002.

text.p: The Philippines has outlined economic targets for the next several years in line with its dream of becoming the newest "Tiger" in the Asian region in the next century, its top finance official said.
In a memorandum dated February 24, 1997 but only released on Monday, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo unveiled his "pole vaulting strategy to the 21st strategy".

At the core of this ambitious target is the rise in tax contributions to 20 percent of gross national product in 2002 from an estimated 17.7 percent in 1998. This would outstrip the present levels of Thailand and Indonesia and edge closer to the level of Malaysia, he said.
"This will enable us to generate fiscal surpluses, cut down inflation and interest rates, boost saving and investment and promote sustainable rapid growth," De Ocampo said.

The national government surplus is envisioned to rise to 37 billion pesos in 2002 from an estimated 16 billion pesos in 1998, while capital expenditures are expected to expand by about 20 to 25 percent yearly.

Inflation is expected to drop to three percent in 2002 from a forecasted 5.5 percent in 1998, and interest rates on the 91-day T-bill rate are seen declining to eight percent in 2002 from an estimated 10.5 percent in 1998, De Ocampo said.
